# Results -- Study 501 (Idiosyncratic-Volatility) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: monthly cross-sectional
sort on rolling 252-day **CAPM-residual** volatility (market beta removed), low-minus-high
(long Q1 lowest-IVOL, short Q5 highest-IVOL), dollar-neutral, one trading-day execution lag,
measured on a large-cap S&P 500 survivor panel. As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 3270 days x 50 tickers | `31bdf138449e` |
| SPY (market proxy) | 3520 days | `b0f3386738bb` |
| Period covered | 2013-01-02 -- 2025-12-31 | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close prices (`auto_adjust=True`). Universe: 50 large-cap
S&P 500 names on a common-history rectangle (common start drifts to 2013 because META/ABBV/AVGO
list ~2012-2013). The panel is survivorship-biased -- current S&P 500 members projected
backwards.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** only companies that survived to 2026 are in the
sample. The high-IVOL names in a survivor large-cap basket (NVDA, TSLA, AMD, META, ...) are
precisely the lottery tickets that *won* -- conditioning on survival is exactly the condition
under which the IVOL puzzle should INVERT. Failed high-IVOL firms (the natural long for the
puzzle's short leg) have been deleted. All results are **upper-bound / direction-biased**
estimates.

## The honest test -- low-minus-high IVOL long-short

IVOL = annualised std of the trailing-252-day OLS residual of each stock's daily excess
return on SPY's daily excess return (CAPM; market beta removed, not raw total vol). Each
month, stocks are sorted into quintiles; we go long the lowest-IVOL quintile (Q1) and short
the highest-IVOL quintile (Q5), dollar-neutral, entering one trading day after the signal.
The Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang (2006) puzzle predicts this **low-minus-high** spread is
**positive** (low IVOL out-earns high IVOL).

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N months | 142 (2014-02 -- 2025-11) |
| GROSS mean (low-minus-high, annualised) | **-21.54%/yr** |
| GROSS vol (annualised) | 18.49%/yr |
| GROSS Sharpe (annual) | -1.164 |
| **GROSS HAC t-stat** | **-4.293** |
| GROSS hit rate (months > 0) | 36.6% |
| GROSS max drawdown | -94.2% |
| **Placebo (sign-flip) p-value** | **0.000** |
| NET mean (after costs) | -22.24%/yr |
| NET HAC t-stat | -4.434 |
| Avg one-sided turnover / month | 0.345 |
| Cost assumption | 5 bps one-way x turnover + 50 bps/yr borrow |

- The puzzle is **REVERSED, not replicated.** The low-minus-high spread is strongly
  **negative** (-21.5%/yr, HAC *t* = **-4.29**) -- the opposite sign to the AHXZ prediction.
  The placebo p-value is 0.000: the negative relation is statistically rock-solid, but it
  points the wrong way for the puzzle.
- High-IVOL stocks **out-earned** low-IVOL stocks by a wide margin on this tape -- the
  classic survivorship inversion (you kept the high-IVOL names that paid off).

## Quintile mean returns (Q1 = lowest IVOL ... Q5 = highest IVOL)

| Quintile | Mean return (annualised) |
|---|--:|
| Q1 (low IVOL) | +13.15%/yr |
| Q2 | +16.69%/yr |
| Q3 | +15.12%/yr |
| Q4 | +20.51%/yr |
| Q5 (high IVOL) | +34.69%/yr |

The series is **increasing** in IVOL -- the mirror image of the AHXZ monotone-*decreasing*
table. Low-IVOL (Q1) earns roughly the market (+13.2% vs SPY +14.3%); high-IVOL (Q5) more
than doubled the market at +34.7%/yr.

## Robustness

**Window sweep (gross low-minus-high HAC t):**

| IVOL window | Mean (%/yr) | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| 126d | -21.10 | -4.30 |
| 189d | -19.79 | -4.19 |
| 252d | -21.54 | -4.29 |
| 504d | -22.60 | -4.27 |

**Quantile-count sweep (gross HAC t):**

| Quantiles | Mean (%/yr) | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| 3 | -14.13 | -3.87 |
| 5 | -21.54 | -4.29 |
| 10 | -27.35 | -3.34 |

The negative spread is invariant to the estimation window and to the number of buckets --
this is not a knob-tuning artifact. It is a stable feature of the survivor basket.

## Synthetic positive control (engine faithfulness)

A deterministic panel with a *planted* IVOL puzzle (low-IVOL alpha > 0, high-IVOL alpha < 0).
The engine recovers a spread monotone in the planted premium and reaches |t| > 2 once the
planted effect is large enough -- proving the engine can detect the AHXZ sign **when it is
present**:

| Planted premium | low-minus-high (%/yr) | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| -0.06 | -2.74 | -0.56 |
| 0.00 | -0.54 | -0.11 |
| +0.06 | +1.65 | +0.34 |
| +0.12 | +3.85 | +0.79 |
| +0.30 | +10.15 | +2.39 |
| +0.50 | +17.44 | +4.11 |

The control is a power/faithfulness check only -- it does NOT support the real-tape stamp. On
the real tape the engine returns the *opposite* sign, so the verdict reflects the market (and
the survivor basket), not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE (for the puzzle).** The AHXZ puzzle predicts a positive low-minus-high
  spread; on this survivor large-cap panel the spread is strongly **negative** (-21.5%/yr,
  HAC *t* = -4.29, placebo p = 0.000). The puzzle as stated does **not** replicate -- it
  inverts. There is a statistically overwhelming IVOL-return relation, but it has the wrong
  sign for the published anomaly, so the puzzle's signal is NONE here.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The only "edge" available is the reversed leg (long high-IVOL),
  which is a survivorship artifact: you can only trade it if you already know which high-IVOL
  names survive. Sharpe of the puzzle spread is -1.16; max drawdown -94%. Net of costs it is
  marginally worse than gross. Nothing here is investable as a forward strategy.
- **Survivorship -- Named.** The inversion is the textbook survivorship mechanism: a basket of
  *surviving* large-caps over-weights the high-IVOL lottery winners (NVDA/TSLA/AMD/META). On a
  broad, delisting-complete universe AHXZ document the puzzle's *negative* IVOL-return
  relation; our survivor sample flips the sign. Direction-biased upper bound.
